terms.definition: A living thing made of a single cell that has no nucleus and no membrane-bound compartments inside it — bacteria are prokaryotes.
The region inside a bacterial cell where its circular DNA sits, loosely coiled — it does the job of a nucleus but isn't wrapped in its own membrane.
The gel-like fluid that fills the inside of a cell, where the DNA, ribosomes, and chemical reactions all sit together.
A tiny molecular machine that reads genetic instructions and builds proteins — bacterial ribosomes are a different size than human ones.
A rigid outer layer around most bacterial cells that gives them shape and protects them from bursting or collapsing.
The tough, mesh-like molecule that makes up the cell wall in most bacteria.
A long, whip-like structure that spins like a propeller to help a bacterial cell swim toward food or away from danger.
The way most bacteria reproduce: one cell copies its DNA and splits in half, making two identical new cells.
